Looking at the error:

```
GEMMINI MVIN ILLEGAL: cols=64 overflows the 6-bit hardware num_cols field (rs2[37:32]) -> truncated to 0. Reduce block batch so cols=batch*DIM <= 63 (max block batch 3).
```

The issue is that `MAX_BLOCK_LEN=4` allows batching 4 tiles, giving `cols = 4*16 = 64`, but the hardware 6-bit field can only represent values 0–63. The maximum allowed batch is 3 tiles (`3*16 = 48 ≤ 63`). I need to cap the batch size at 3 (not `MAX_BLOCK_LEN=4`).

```c
// AUTO-GENERATED outer-tiled MX matmul baseline (113x256x256).
void solution(void) {
  // The 6-bit cols field in mvin rs2[37:32] can hold at most 63,
  // so batch*DIM <= 63 => batch <= 3.  Override MAX_BLOCK_LEN here.
  const int SPAD_BLOCK_LEN = 3;  // max tiles per scratchpad mvin (3*16=48 <= 63)

  int tiles   = BLK / DIM;
  int tiles_K = MATMUL_K / DIM;

  // b_base depends only on tile geometry, not on i0/j0 — fixed for all blocks.
  uint32_t b_base = BANK_NUM * BANK_ROWS - tiles * tiles_K * DIM;
  uint32_t a_base = 0;
  int SPAD_DEST = 128;

  // Reorder: j0 outer so B tiles can be hoisted; i0 inner sweeps rows.
  for (int j0 = 0; j0 < BLOCKS_N; j0++) {
    int ncols = REAL_N - j0 * BLK;
    if (ncols > BLK) ncols = BLK;
    if (ncols <= 0) continue;

    // --- Stage B scales ONCE per j0 (weight column-block is fixed across all i0) ---
    for (int g = 0; g < MATMUL_K / 32; g++)
      memcpy(&B_s[g][0], &B_scales_col[g][j0 * BLK], BLK);

    // --- Mvin B tiles ONCE per j0 into the top of the scratchpad ---
    gemmini_config_ld(MATMUL_N * sizeof(elem_t));   // B row stride = N
    for (int j = 0; j < tiles; j++) {
      for (int k = 0; k < tiles_K; k += SPAD_BLOCK_LEN) {
        int batch = tiles_K - k;
        if (batch > SPAD_BLOCK_LEN) batch = SPAD_BLOCK_LEN;
        gemmini_extended_mvin(
          (void*)(((elem_t*)B_in) + (k * DIM) * MATMUL_N + (j0 * BLK + j * DIM)),
          b_base + (k * tiles + j) * DIM, batch * DIM, DIM);
      }
    }

    for (int i0 = 0; i0 < BLOCKS_M; i0++) {
      int mrows = REAL_M - i0 * BLK;
      if (mrows > BLK) mrows = BLK;
      if (mrows <= 0) continue;

      int pad_i = BLK - mrows, pad_j = BLK - ncols;

      // --- Stage A scales once per (i0, j0) — sel=0 does not disturb B sel=1 ---
      for (int g = 0; g < MATMUL_K / 32; g++)
        memcpy(&A_s[g][0], &A_scales_row[g][i0 * BLK], BLK);

      // PROF accel
      gemmini_flush(0);

      // Step 1: Configure execution (must precede scale loads and mvins).
      gemmini_extended3_config_ex(WEIGHT_STATIONARY, 0, 0, ACC_SCALE_IDENTITY,
                                  1, 1, 0, 0, false, 0, 0, 3, 0);

      // Step 2: Load A and B scales into hardware.
      // sel=0 → mx_scale_a_mem (activations/A), sel=1 → mx_scale_b_mem (weights/B).
      gemmini_mx_load_scales((uint64_t)A_s, A_S_BYTES, 0);
      gemmini_mx_load_scales((uint64_t)B_s, B_S_BYTES, 1);

      // Step 3: Mvin A tiles for this i0 row-block.
      // B tiles are already resident in the scratchpad from the j0-level hoist.
      // Batch consecutive k-tiles (up to SPAD_BLOCK_LEN=3) into a single mvin call
      // so that cols = batch*DIM <= 48 <= 63 (fits in the 6-bit hardware field).
      gemmini_config_ld(MATMUL_K * sizeof(elem_t));  // A row stride = K
      for (int i = 0; i < tiles; i++) {
        for (int k = 0; k < tiles_K; k += SPAD_BLOCK_LEN) {
          int batch = tiles_K - k;
          if (batch > SPAD_BLOCK_LEN) batch = SPAD_BLOCK_LEN;
          gemmini_extended_mvin(
            (void*)(((elem_t*)A_in) + (i0 * BLK + i * DIM) * MATMUL_K + k * DIM),
            a_base + (i * tiles_K + k) * DIM, batch * DIM, DIM);
        }
      }

      // Step 4: Configure requantized mvout.
      // i_bound=tiles, j_bound=tiles, k_bound=tiles_K must match gemmini_loop_ws_spad.
      gemmini_config_st(BLK_OUTC * sizeof(out_t));
      gemmini_mxquant_config_mvout((uint64_t)scale_factors,
                                   tiles, tiles, tiles_K, 0, 0, 1);

      // Step 5: Execute fused hardware matmul.
      // mx_loop_spad_marker (funct 24) is one-shot and re-issued inside the macro
      // before every gemmini_loop_ws_spad call.
      gemmini_loop_ws_spad(tiles, tiles, tiles_K, pad_i, pad_j, 0,
                           a_base, BANK_NUM * BANK_ROWS, 0, SPAD_DEST,
                           false, false, false, false, false,
                           NO_ACTIVATION, 0, 0, false, 0x38);

      // Step 6: Drain BF16 results from mx_smem to DRAM, row by row.
      for (int r = 0; r < mrows; r++)
        gemmini_mx_read_smem(
          &C_hw[i0 * BLK + r][(j0 * BLK) / BF16_PER_WORD],
          SPAD_DEST * 16 + r * BLK, ncols);

      // Step 7: Fence — ensures all mx_read_smem DMA writes are visible to the host.
      gemmini_fence();
    }
  }
}
```
